scope: MEAS: independent numerical, report/source, published bar-map, actual-sheet and visual review; not aural review.

report.finding: Report agrees with final checks, 7188 performed events / 186 bar occurrences, 11 source-section aggregates, exact trio endings and eight-page pack. It distinguishes the 5757 canonical-attack audit from repeat-expanded counts, omits separately licensed analytical lyrics and rejects the wrong broad-window endpoints.

barMap.finding: All 7188 note bar/voice indices resolve, durations are positive and performed bar times strictly increase. Actual SVG/index sets are exactly 1–165. Pages 1, 4, 6 and 8 were inspected. Targeted magnification confirms genuine opening repeat dots at 87, closing dots after first ending 108 and distinct 1./2. brackets at 108/109; an unprocessed-marker warning is not evidence of a missing visible repeat. Listen sections use seconds, without structured bar pointers.

overlays.finding: No gross pitch/order mismatch identified across the corrected opening, both trio traversals, weak-harmonic regions and complete ending. The source begins near 0.68 s rather than the louder later repetition, and retains the actual final A-flat arrival near 292.043 s rather than the earlier cadence. Written duration and estimated decay end are not measured physical releases.

source.finding: Published metadata correctly states that separately licensed analytical lyrics are omitted from this derivative; none were asserted as CC0 analysis.

version.finding: Complete third movement in coherent order 1–108, 87–107, 109–165. The first ending is not repeated on traversal two. Source transpositions and genuine section groups are retained without inventing extra bass-register instruments or a silent-part substitute. No gross cut/arrangement mismatch identified.
version.physicalPerformingEdition: Unknown; the identified transcription/scan is not claimed as the recorded orchestra’s physical performing copy.

limitations: MEAS: No aural review, build or browser integration check performed by VerS. Recurrence and visual correspondence support the traversal, not exact identity of every recorded note, instrumental doubling or physical release.
